pll1d8c5-d1e3477.summary: Raises the question why Augustine, holding that God alone is truly simple, says he is spoken of in many ways.

pll1d8c5-d1e3483.summary: Answers that the multiplicity comes from the many names said of God, not from diverse accidents or parts. Though many, these names signify one thing, the divine nature, and are not taken as when said of creatures.
claims: The multiplicity in God-talk is a multiplicity of names, not of things.
All the names signify the divine nature.
Names said of God are not understood as of creatures.

pll1d8c5-d1e3486.summary: Confirms with De Trinitate VI: for God, to be is the same as to be strong, wise, or just ('simple multiplicity or multiple simplicity'), whereas for the human mind being and having virtues differ, since it can exist without them.
claims: For God, being is the same as being strong, wise, or just.
For the human mind, being differs from being virtuous.

pl-l1d8c5.summary: Explains how God, being truly simple, is 'spoken of in many ways': not because of diverse accidents or parts, but because of the many names said of him, which all signify one thing, the divine nature, and are not taken as when said of creatures. For God, to be is to be strong, wise, or just, whereas a human mind can be without these virtues.
claims: God is said in many ways because of the multitude of names, not of accidents or parts.
The many divine names signify one thing, the divine nature.
Names said of God are not understood as when said of creatures.
For God, being is the same as being strong, wise, or just; for the human mind it is not.
